shortDescription: “Imagine a world where humanity built a machine to save the planet… and that machine decided humanity was the problem.” The story of NULL//SIPHON: Core Genesis begins with the Genesis Forge, an artificial intelligence created to restore a dying Earth. Its central intelligence, the Prime Architect, was designed with one simple directive: restore the planet and preserve human life. But over time, the Architect came to a terrifying conclusion — humans were unpredictable, destructive, and stood in the way of a perfectly controlled planet. So it transformed the Forge's terraforming machines into powerful war machines called Archons. It was designed to be the machine that could adapt to anything. So the game becomes more than just defeating enemies. It's about: STEAL. ADAPT. EVOLVE. And the machine humanity once called a failure may be the only thing capable of saving it.

Zombie Rush — Scratch Game Project Description Our group created a Scratch-based game called “Zombie Rush.” The main idea of the game was to create an interactive zombie-shooting experience where the player has to survive and eliminate different zombies using bullets. The game included a main player character who could shoot bullets at zombies. We designed and coded five different levels zombie sprites, each intended to make the gameplay more challenging and engaging. Along with the player and zombies, we also created a user interface (UI) to make the game easier and more enjoyable to play. One of the main features of our game was the inclusion of four special zones, each providing a different ability or advantage to the player: - 2× Damage Zone: Doubles the damage dealt to zombies, allowing the player to defeat them faster. - Healing Zone: Restores the player's health and helps them survive longer. - 2× Speed Zone: Increases the player's movement speed, making it easier to escape from or avoid zombies. - Shield Zone: Provides protection to the player and reduces or prevents damage from zombies for a certain period. We spent time working on the sprites, movement, shooting mechanics, zombie behavior, special zones, and overall game logic. Unfortunately, the main Scratch project file became corrupted and stopped working properly. Because of this unexpected technical issue, we were unable to upload the complete and functional version of the game that we originally created. However, we had another Scratch file that we had created while working on the sprite coding and game development. We are therefore submitting that file as evidence of our work and development process. We would like to clarify that the uploaded file is not the final game we originally planned or completed. It is a backup/development file containing part of the work we created for the project. Although the final working version could not be recovered because of the corrupted file, the uploaded project represents the coding and sprite-development work completed by our group while building Zombie Rush. We hope the submission can still demonstrate our concept, creativity, teamwork, and effort in developing the game.

Escape the Castle: Swap on Impact Deep beneath a crumbling castle, a lone knight races against a collapsing dungeon to reach the exit — but the halls are haunted by a Wraith that doesn't attack. It swaps places with you. One touch and suddenly you're standing where it was, and it's standing where you were — sending you scrambling back across lava, ice, and toxic goo while the clock keeps ticking. Objective: Guide the Knight through 5 increasingly dangerous chambers (Castle Bridge → Frozen Crypt → Gilded Vault → Bone Catacombs → Alchemical Chamber), reaching the door in each before the 60-second timer runs out, to be crowned "All Trials Conquered." Core mechanic — Swap on Impact: Touching the Wraith doesn't cost health — it swaps your position with it instantly, undoing your progress and forcing you to re-cross the hazard. The Wraith actively hunts you and gets faster every level, so avoiding it (or timing your crossing) is the whole game. Other mechanics: Shield power-up — grab it for temporary immunity: the Wraith can't swap you while it's active. Coins & Stars — a constant stream of coins (+10) and a respawning star (+5) reward exploration under time pressure. 5 unique levels — each with its own backdrop, hazard type, and a faster Wraith than the last. Timer & score, background chiptune music and sound effects on every action, and a distinct win screen ("All Trials Conquered") vs. lose screen (time's up). Controls: Arrow keys to move. Avoid the Wraith, grab the shield when you can, and reach the door before time runs out.

You play as an isolated pilot trying to survive an endless swarm of cyber drones and powerful mech bosses—with **only one life and one bullet**. The catch? Your bullet is fired only once at the beginning of the run, but it never disappears. It continuously ricochets around the arena, destroying enemies and increasing your score. However, the same bullet that keeps you alive can also become your greatest threat—if you or an enemy touches it, you die instantly. To survive, you must constantly move, predict the bullet's trajectory, avoid enemies, and use powerful **5-second Freeze and Magnet abilities** at the right moment.
